incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: realtime-p99-regression-detector in us-central1 for /v1/streaming. p99 = 1.2s (baseline 0.28s), p95 = 420ms. No increase in 5xx in metrics alert, but streaming stalls reported. Paging Devon (oncall).
Devon (oncall): acknowledged, I'm on it. grabbing dashboards now. ping me with link & quick checks.
Alex (sre): looking — live Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming/latency-overview?orgId=1&from=now-15m&to=now :eyes:
Alex (sre): p99 spike aligns with a gradual increase in inflight concurrent streams from a burst job at 14:02 UTC. CPU on serving-nodes rose ~60% and queue latency spiked. No obvious OOMs.
Devon (oncall): any 5xx or tail errors? support?
Sam (support): users reporting stalled streams (client sees keepalive but no tokens) — about ~8% of streaming sessions in last 10m. No mass 5xx in normal endpoints.
Maria (runtime): adding notes — we recently rolled kvcache v2 to canary (10% traffic) in us-central1 at 13:55 UTC. That rollout touched async-prefetch and cache-eviction timing. Could be a regression in cache warming leading to tail stalls.
Olivia (product): customer-impact: initial reports from two enterprise customers using streaming chat in production. SLA impact if sustained. tagging CS to prepare comms.
Jordan (eng): quick triage steps I recommend:
1) Confirm if canary traffic fraction spiked (k/v mismatch)
2) If yes, route traffic away from canary (traffic-split -> 0%)
3) If not, reduce batch max_tokens to avoid long encode spikes
I'll run step 1 now.
Alex (sre): runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/latency/streaming-tail-stalls — follow "canary kvcache" section.
Devon (oncall): @Maria — can you check the canary pool and logs for eviction exceptions? Maria: on it.
Maria (runtime): quick grep on cache logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:03:12Z WARN kvcache:evict key=ctx-abc size=0 last_access=2m
2026-03-15T14:03:12Z ERROR kvcache:prefetch failed: timeout
```
prefetch timeouts line up with spike window.
Maria (runtime): metrics: canary_pool_prefetch_fail_rate went 0.2% -> 12% between 13:55 and 14:05.
Jordan (eng): that matches. initiating rollback of canary to 0% traffic and switch to stable kvcache v1 for this pool.
infra-bot: executing traffic-split update: service=streaming-us-central1, from_canary=10% -> 0%. change-id=chg-9876
infra-bot: deployment job started -> finished :white_check_mark:
Devon (oncall): confirm telemetry after rollback, watching p95/p99 now.
Alex (sre): immediate dashboard shows p99 falling from 1.2s -> 520ms in 90s. p95 back to ~300ms. streams-stalled gauge down from 8% -> 2%.
Sam (support): customers updated: two affected customers noticed partial recovery. CS preparing status note.
Olivia (product): good. let's keep rollback as mitigation while runtime investigates root cause of prefetch timeouts.
Maria (runtime): gathering deeper logs and reproducer. suspicion: race in eviction + prefetch under load; sending debug build to canary infra in a non-customer pool for repro.
Jordan (eng): additional mitigation: temporarily lower max_batch_size for streaming encoder from 64 -> 32 to reduce processing latency. rolling change to 25% traffic now.
infra-bot: config-update: streaming-encoder.max_batch_size=32 target=25% -> applied.
Alex (sre): note: reducing batch size will increase token compute costs but reduces tail latency; good short-term mitigation.
Devon (oncall): monitoring for next 20m. if p99 stabilizes under 500ms and stalls <1% we can close paging. otherwise escalate to full incident.
Sam (support): I'll keep ticket threads open with customers and escalate if they see regressions.
Maria (runtime): captured heap/profile and trace spans for failed prefetch path, posted to crashpad: https://crash.redwood/internal/evt/5555
Jordan (eng): plan: root-cause runbook items — increase prefetch timeout OR add backpressure to prefetch queue, plus fix eviction race. will open PR with tests.
Devon (oncall): current status update in 5m, thanks all. :thumbsup:
Alex (sre): small follow-up: where we saw spike, there was also a surge of long-running requests from an internal replay job — @Jordan can we add a rate-limiter for internal replay traffic to avoid noise in production pools?
Jordan (eng): yep, I'll add a guard. quick patch in staging then promote.
Devon (oncall): final note for now: pages acknowledged, rollback -> p99 improved, interim mitigations applied (batch size, canary rollback). Keeping thread open until metrics stable for 20m. :eyes:
incident-bot: Incident paging status: acknowledged by oncall, severity: p95/p99-slo-breach potential, incident-id=inc-20260315-01."
